Then we got the chocolate lava cake, which was great to share and decadent.

Overall had a good experience.

text.text:
Service needs improvement, a lot of improvement. As with any business It starts from the top.  This review is no different than what the other reviewers have said in other reviews. I am not sure who rated this place as 4 or 5 starts. I think the 4 and 5 stars they receive are bots.

These are the areas of service I noticed needed improvement.

I had to ask for napkins. Had to get the ketchup myself. Isn’t it common place for a server to ask if you want ketchup or any other condiments when you order fries. Additionally he never asked to refill my soda. Free refills are supposed to be included. (Same as other reviews, they don’t care)
Never asked us how our meal was going or if we needed anything. Overall he wasn’t very pleasant just going through the motions. Just being honest.
Burger was good. Not excellent or great. Just good.
Cutlery came in its own paper packaging. I guess that means it was clean. Suspicious considering the quality of the service, I question the cleanliness of the cutlery.

At least the the TVs had entertaining videos. Distractions.

Don’t get me wrong. I tipped the guy anyway because I am a nice guy and worked in the restaurant industry. We went with the 2 for 25 meal special. With sodas and tip came out to 40 something.

UPDATE later tonight. 1 hr later. Food gave me a stomach ache. Not eating here again.

text.text: This was my first time at Spyce & I have to say it was nice. Great music & even better a live DJ. There were alot of great aspects to it, along w/ some needs improvement. I'll start w/ the decor which was beautiful. There were chandeliers everywhere w/ purple & blue lighting. On the tables were votive candles. There were different dining locations. We were seated by the bar near the Dj booth in booth which made for intimate dining. I had a Peach Sensation and my husband had a Passion fruit mojito. He said his was tasty & as for me mine was just ok. I asked for a lime to add some tartness to balance out the over powering sweetness from the simple syrup. We then ordered a pitcher of the Passion fruit mojito and it was a good choice. For appiziter we ordered a sample platter which came with chicken/beef/pork empanadas, fried pork & fried chicken & calamari. We enjoyed it but there was a old oil smell to it, they just need to change the oil frequently. Next we had the Shrimp Mofongo, had good flavor but the plantains were not mashed enough. My husband had Salmon & mashed potatoes, it was delicious. Overall, drinks should be made well balanced, &replacing oil frequently makes for the best flavor to all fried goodies...

text.text:
Took my kids to the Chuck E. Cheese near Astoria (in Long Island City) for a birthday outing. The kids had a blast playing arcade games and collecting tickets—it’s definitely designed with young children in mind. The pizza and wings were just okay—not gourmet but acceptable.
However, the noisiness and smell near the entry and play areas were distracting, and several game machines were out of order. It took a while for our food order to arrive, and the staff seemed overwhelmed. For the price, it felt a bit underwhelming.
Great for energetic kids who want carnival-style fun, but be prepared for a chaotic environment and spotty service

text.text:
If we could give 6/5 stars, this would be the place we do it.

Food, service, and a good time never fail here! Even after the change in ownership Doyle’s Corner is a local favorite with amazing food and service. They even re-introduced trivia nights, karaoke nights, and other fun events to their weekly schedule.

We’re big fans of their specials menu and love when they have the pork chops w/ mash and veggies. Between their wings, burgers, Sheppard’s Pie, spare ribs, even soups, you cannot go wrong here.

Be aware though- this is mostly a beer bar. Some wines and spiked ciders available but minimal cocktails if you’re into that.

text.text: The restaurant has a area for sitting if you want to eat and another section if you want to drink at the bar. We had a nice lady who attended us and was quick with our orders. The food was pretty good. The mac and cheese was very cheesy. I thought it was cool they brought the burger with the toppings on the side so it didn’t get soggy and you can add it yourself after.  The food is made fresh everyday so I recommend trying it out.

High expectations, but not impressed with this visit. Wednesday early dinner , 7/23/25, 5pm.
No issue with availability and service, very attentive.
Chicken dish with sauce ok, but asparagus flimsy and green bean sized while mashed potatoes served ice cream scoop and lacking in flavor.
Long awaited favorite of mine, fish and chips.
Fish better than most in area, still lacking in wow factor while the (chips) were a flimsy mess , no crisp or seasoning.
As to beer, Stella was fine but Blue Moon dark and flat.
Better luck next time.

text.text: If you're looking for a traditional Irish neighborhood pub with better-than-usual food, good drinks, friendly people, comfortable seating at the bar and booths, and sports on big-screen TVs, this is the place. Highly recommended. Excellent for lunch (with an inexpensive selection of lunch specials), dinner (also moderately priced), or just drinks. The owner, Mike Peacock, is usually there greeting customers and runs a great operation.

text.text: I really wanted to like this place since I live locally in Astoria, but my first experience was incredibly disappointing. I stopped in during happy hour and sat at the bar, hoping to grab a margarita and check out the menu specials. Unfortunately, I was completely ignored. I sat there over 10 minutes while the bartender gave his exclusive attention to one woman in front of him. He actively avoided looking down the bar to check on other patrons or see who else needed a drink. It felt like he was intentionally catering to a specific person while entirely shutting out newcomers. I ended up getting up and leaving without ever being acknowledged. As a local, it’s a shame to be made to feel unwelcome. Won’t be back.
